blocks.text: SAT 15 AUG. Sled access day. Sled push and pull remain sandbag friction-overloaded (since 3 Jul) — splits compare to 8 Aug and to each other, NOT to race benchmarks.

THE REVISED BIRMINGHAM MECHANISM — read this before you start. Race-file HR: Run 1 143.5 -> SkiErg 128.1 -> roxzone 120.8 -> Run 2 at 5:03/km, THE SAME PACE AS RUN 1, HR 150.8 -> Sled Push 5:14 of work against 2:59 at Cardiff -> every run after pinned 178-182. HR fell through the ski because SkiErg is upper-body and non-weight-bearing; it built a lactate cost the HR trace could not show. The ski loaded it. RUN 2 AT UNCHANGED PACE IS THE DECISION THAT SPENT IT. The sled push is where the time went.

REMOVED FROM THE 8 AUG BRIEF: 'can you hold run 1 pace straight off the ski'. That instruction rehearsed the failure. Run 2 is held at CONTROLLED pace regardless of how good the ski felt. That restraint is the skill being trained.

PEAK HR IS NOT THE METRIC. On 8 Aug the runs held 253-258W against CP 261 — 97-99% of threshold power — and still capped at HR 162, because a 3:00 block never lets HR arrive. Peak HR here measures block length, not effort.

SUCCESS CRITERIA, in order: (1) SLED PUSH SPLIT — the primary readout, the station that collapsed at Birmingham. (2) RESTART HR — HR at the top of run 4 no more than 6 bpm above the top of run 2. (3) FOUR RUN SPLITS INSIDE 5 SECONDS. (4) RATCHET SHAPE — you want climb-then-hold, roughly 155 -> 165 -> 170 -> 170. Climbing and still climbing at run 4 means you are rehearsing Birmingham. On 8 Aug it read 147 -> 158 -> 162 -> 162, which decelerated into a plateau at 162; the target band for a well-executed race is 168-174.
SKI: one notch harder than 8 Aug, not two. The 8 Aug PWA RPE was 7, not the 4 the old file recorded. Enough to leave a real cost, not enough to reproduce the failure.

RUN PACE: 5:25-5:35/km = 10.8-11.1 km/h, roughly 248-256W at CP 261. START RUN 1 AT 10.8. On 8 Aug you started at 10.98 and the two slowest runs followed — 16s spread across four when the stated test was four flat.

2026-09-19.title: CFG Intermediate - 6 x 800m + 6 stations + 200m finish = VO2max session

blocks.text: SAT 19 SEP. CFG INTERMEDIATE (confirmed 5 Sep). Format: 800m run then station, x6, then 200m finish - 5.0 km running total. Stations in order: tyre flips 60m (~60 kg) / slam ball wall overs 15kg x20 / farmers walk 14kg 120m / burpee broad jumps 60m / sandbag lunges 15kg 60m / DB snatches 10kg x30 each arm. THIS IS THE WEEK'S VO2max SESSION - not extra, not a race. PRIMARY GOAL: even-paced VO2max stimulus - 6 reps inside a 5 s band, rep 6 no slower than rep 1. Reps 1-2 held at the slow end. First VO2-intensity running since 2 Jul: govern the early reps, no leaderboard.

RUN TARGETS (anchors from Mon 14 TT - if CP moved, re-scale). Default CP 261W / 5:15 / LTHR 178. Reps 1-4: 275-285W (105-109% CP). ON YOUR POD THAT LANDS SOMEWHERE IN 5:00-5:15/km (~4:00-4:12 per 800) DEPENDING ON THE DAY - NOT 4:40s. Evidence: 10 Aug 5x1km 5:03-5:13 at 265-293W; 7 Sep Arona 262W = 5:20 and 275W = 5:15 (day 3 post-race, 18C). The POWER is the target; the pace is whatever it comes out as. If the Mon 14 TT moves CP, re-scale the band off the new number, not this pace. Reps 5-6: free ONLY if 1-4 were in band. 200m finish: as hard as you like, nothing follows it. HR: end-of-rep HR climbs through the session and sits above 178 from rep 3 on. If it is there in rep 1 you went out too hot. STEER BY POWER, not pace. Restart rule: HR at the start of the next 800 no higher than at the end of the previous one, and settled at rep pace inside 200m. If you cannot hit rep pace by 200m the station was too fast, not the rep.

STATION SPLIT. GOVERN the three hinge-from-floor stations - tyre flips, wall overs, DB snatches - none are HYROX patterns and the loaded-hinge-under-fatigue question is self-managed now: symptom RPE is the only governor. MOVE THROUGH farmers walk and lunges at a controlled pace (both well under race load - you race 2x24kg/200m and 20kg/100m). HOLD burpee broad jumps steady - biggest HR driver on the sheet and it sits before run 5. Effort RPE and spinal symptom RPE logged SEPARATELY at every station. Symptom RPE >2 at any station = stop chasing the station, walk it through, jog the remaining reps. Spinal checkpoint outranks the clock.

Per flip: feet close, hips LOW, chest on the tyre - make it a squat-drive not a hinge - exhale on the drive, flip it over, don't catch or press it, step up to the next. Break it into blocks of 10 with 2-3 breaths between - 20-30s total cost, buys a clean back for the other five stations. Target ~3:30-4:30. Log effort + spinal RPE.

prerun.text: PRE-RUN — ~9 min, in order. Spine-neutral throughout: no standing toe touches, no seated forward folds, no supine knees-to-chest. Press START on the first step, it auto-advances the whole routine.

prerun.label: Knee-to-wall dorsiflexion
prerun.detail: 10 reps/side, 2s hold at end range. Heel down, knee over 2nd toe. Switch at halfway. Note the L/R gap difference.

prerun.label: Ankle circles
prerun.detail: 20 each direction, both sides. Slow, full range.

prerun.label: Bent-knee heel raise
prerun.detail: 15 reps, 2s lower. Soleus — takes the running load, don't skip it.

prerun.label: Single-leg balance hold
prerun.detail: 20s on the weaker ankle only. Eyes open.

prerun.label: Half-kneeling hip flexor
prerun.detail: 30s/side. Squeeze the down-leg glute, tuck the pelvis. Do NOT arch the back to feel it.

prerun.label: 90/90 hip switches
prerun.detail: 8 slow reps. Sit tall, hands behind, chest up. Stop short if the low back rounds to get there.

prerun.label: Leg swings (wall support)
prerun.detail: 12 front/back then 12 lateral per side. Small range first 4, then build. Swing from the hip, trunk braced.

prerun.label: Glute bridge
prerun.detail: 15 reps, 2s squeeze at top, ribs down.

prerun.label: Banded lateral walk
prerun.detail: 10 steps each direction x2. Band above knees, soft knees, no torso lean.

prerun.label: Pogo hops
prerun.detail: 2 x 15. Stiff ankles, minimal knee bend, short ground contact. SKIP on easy days or if flat.

core.text: CORE / TRUNK ENDURANCE - ~16 min. Anti-movement only: resist flexion, extension, rotation and lateral flexion, never produce them. PERMANENTLY OUT with the annular tear: sit-ups, crunches, V-ups, toes-to-bar, GHD sit-ups, weighted Russian twists, loaded side bends, hanging leg raises with a rounded lumbar spine. Repeated end-range loaded lumbar flexion is the specific mechanism that drives nuclear material posteriorly through an annular defect.
TIMING: not within the first hour of waking. Discs are maximally hydrated overnight and the spine is at its most flexion-vulnerable then. Mid-morning or later.

PART A - McGill Big 3, descending pyramid 6 -> 4 -> 2 reps. Every rep is a 10-second hold, ~5s between reps, ~30s between sets. Log effort and symptom RPE as SEPARATE numbers per exercise. Symptom RPE above 2 during or after = hard stop, same rule as the stations.

core.label: Modified curl-up - 6/4/2
core.detail: Hands flat UNDER the lumbar spine, one knee bent one leg straight. Lift head and shoulders barely off the floor - you are bracing, not crunching. No spinal flexion. Swap the bent leg between sets. SPINAL CHECKPOINT.

core.label: Side plank - 6/4/2 per side
core.detail: From the knees if the full version provokes anything. Complete the full pyramid on one side, then the other. Straight line ear-to-hip, ribs down, no sagging or hitching. SPINAL CHECKPOINT.

core.label: Bird dog - 6/4/2
core.detail: Opposite arm and leg, 10s hold, alternate sides within the rep count. Broomstick-flat lumbar spine - do NOT arch to reach further. Reach long, not high. SPINAL CHECKPOINT.

core.text: PART B - loaded anti-movement, 3 sets each. Band or cable. This is the part that progresses by load; Part A progresses by duration only.

core.label: Pallof press - 3 x 8-10/side
core.detail: Stand side-on to the anchor, band at sternum height. Press to full extension and hold 3 seconds resisting the rotation, then return under control. Hips square, no leaning away from the pull.

core.label: Dead bug w/ overhead band - 3 x 8/side
core.detail: Arms hold band tension overhead, ribs pinned down, low back flat to the floor. Lower opposite arm and leg slowly. If the back lifts off the floor, shorten the range - that is the rep limit, not a cue to push through.

core.text: PROGRESSION, in this order and one at a time: (1) pyramid to 8/6/4, (2) holds 10s -> 12s, (3) more band tension on Part B. Never add external load to the Big 3. HOLD STEADY through the w/c 31 Aug deload+taper - that is not the place for a new stimulus. Progress from the Birmingham build, w/c 7 Sep.

hinge_block.text: HINGE BLOCK - 15-20 min, once per week, in front of the station work (standalone on its first outing, Fri 11 Sep). This is NOT a strength session. It is a fresh, controlled dose of loaded hinge so the lunge ladder is not the only hinge exposure you get. Purpose: spinal graded exposure. Log effort and symptom RPE separately. Symptom >2 = stop the block AND drop the station session to race volume.

hinge_block.label: Barbell RDL 3 x 6 @ 50 kg
hinge_block.detail: Neutral spine, hinge to just below the knee, 2 s down. 50 kg is the restart weight - hold it for two weeks before adding. 90 s between sets. SPINAL CHECKPOINT.

hinge_block.label: Single-arm farmers carry 24 kg - 3 x 40 m per side
hinge_block.detail: Anti-lateral-flexion. Tall, ribs down, no lean. Swap sides without putting the bell down if grip allows. 60 s between rounds. SPINAL CHECKPOINT.

ladder_protocol.text: OVER-VOLUME LADDER PROTOCOL - applies to every ladder session. FIXED FOR THE WHOLE BLOCK: BBJ lane 20 m out-and-back (log the lane length if RAW forces something else - a different lane is a different session). Sandbag lunge sets of 25 m. Wall ball sets of 25. Rest 45 s between sets, 3 min walk between stations. Stations in RACE ORDER: BBJ first, then lunges INTO wall balls with only the 3 min walk between - the wall balls are supposed to arrive on legs the lunges have already used.

WHAT TO LOG: time per set, every set. Progress is NOT total time. Progress is total distance/reps going up while the LAST set stays within a few seconds of the FIRST. If the last set is >15% slower than the first, the volume was too high - hold this step next time rather than climbing.

SPINAL RPE: effort and symptom logged separately at the HALFWAY point and the END of lunges and of wall balls, plus end of BBJ. Symptom >2 at any checkpoint = stop that station, finish nothing else loaded, and the ladder holds at the previous step. Same rule as the race.

sled_entry_rehearsal.text: SLED-ENTRY REHEARSAL - the ski:run:sled:run drill. NOT sled conditioning and NOT a session to empty. Purpose: rehearse arriving at the sled with HR headroom and recovering on the run AFTER it. Readout is TWO HR numbers per round - HR the instant you start pushing, and HR at the START of the run after - NOT a time. RAW sled != race sled, so absolute HR won't transfer; you're training the pattern (ski easy, run controlled, arrive calm, recover on the run), not chasing a number. MEASURED ARRIVAL TARGET (12 Sep ceiling test): ~158-160 into the sled - above ~160 the PUSH itself slows even though the run still recovers, and the push is the protected station. Race/rehearse BELOW 160, not the 173 run-settle ceiling. If you arrive at the sled hot, DO NOT chill it away - log it and fix the ski / run-2 pacing next round. Rescuing a hot entry hides the exact signal you came for. Opens the w/c 21 station day in front of the ladder, weekly thereafter.

sled_entry_rehearsal.label: Warm-up 10 min easy + 3 x 20s strides
sled_entry_rehearsal.detail: HR <=148. Strides 20s, 60s walk between. Once, before the rounds.

sled_entry_rehearsal.text: NOW 2 ROUNDS of the block below (build to 3 once familiar), continuous within a round. 2-3 min easy walk/jog between rounds.

sled_entry_rehearsal.label: SkiErg 500m - controlled
sled_entry_rehearsal.detail: Race effort, damper 6. Come off composed, NOT gasping. Gasping off the ski = you rehearsed the mistake. ~1:55-2:05.

sled_entry_rehearsal.label: Run 400m - race pace
sled_entry_rehearsal.detail: ~5:30/km, steered by the watch NOT feel. This is the run-2 rehearsal: the job is to NOT speed up because the ski felt fine.

sled_entry_rehearsal.label: Sled push 25m (2 x 12.5m) - straight on, no pause
sled_entry_rehearsal.detail: Glance at the watch the INSTANT you start pushing and LOG THAT HR = number one. Race weight if RAW loads to it, else the standard sled - log the load once so rounds compare, do NOT chase a metres/split target. Controlled, not a grind. SPINAL CHECKPOINT - symptom separate from effort.

sled_entry_rehearsal.label: Run 400m - controlled - PASS/FAIL
sled_entry_rehearsal.detail: LOG HR at the START of this run = number two. Settles within 100-150m = you managed the entry. Still 175+ = you arrived with no headroom, rein in the ski/run-2 next round.

sled_entry_rehearsal.text: LOG PER ROUND: HR entering the sled, HR restarting the run after, sled load, spinal symptom RPE. Reading it: HR entering the sled drifting UP round to round = ski/run-2 creeping too hard. Times will lie on RAW's kit - the HR pair is the whole measurement.

sled_ceiling_test.text: SLED CEILING TEST - a DIAGNOSTIC, not a weekly session. Purpose: find the ARRIVAL heart rate above which the sled push degrades AND you can't settle on the run after. That number is your sled ceiling - you race BELOW it. Fatigue-version companion to sled_entry_rehearsal: same station, opposite question (that one = arrive controlled; this = arrive hot on purpose and find where it breaks). Run ONCE to establish, re-check every 3-4 weeks or after a CP change. Do NOT hammer it weekly - grinding a sled while redlined just rehearses the failure.

RUN IT FRESH-ISH so the pre-loads are the ONLY fatigue - do not stack on a ladder/long-run day or the arrival HRs are contaminated. Push is not a hinge = low spinal cost, but log symptom RPE as standard. METHOD: 3 rounds, each = a cardiovascular pre-load to an ASCENDING HR band, straight onto the sled, then a run. Push at consistent RACE INTENT every round (committed, not sprinting) - the ONLY thing changing is how hot you arrive. Rest to near-baseline between rounds. Pre-loads are ski/row/run ONLY - no burpees/hinge, keep it cardiovascular and off the spine.

sled_ceiling_test.label: R1 PRE-LOAD - 400-500m SkiErg controlled-hard
sled_ceiling_test.detail: Aim to arrive at the sled ~150-155. Straight on, no pause.

sled_ceiling_test.label: R1 Sled push 25m (2x12.5m) - race intent
sled_ceiling_test.detail: LOG: arrival HR (instant you start pushing) + time for the 25m + did it feel smooth? Race weight if RAW loads to it, else standard sled - log the load. SPINAL CHECKPOINT.

sled_ceiling_test.label: R1 Run 400m controlled
sled_ceiling_test.detail: LOG: HR at the start + metres to settle to pace. Then rest 2-3 min to near baseline.

sled_ceiling_test.label: R2 PRE-LOAD - 500m Ski hard + 250m Row hard
sled_ceiling_test.detail: (or ~3 min hard erg). Aim to arrive ~168-172. Straight onto the sled.

sled_ceiling_test.label: R2 Sled push 25m - race intent
sled_ceiling_test.detail: LOG: arrival HR + 25m time + smooth, or choppy/gasping between the 12.5s? SPINAL CHECKPOINT.

sled_ceiling_test.label: R2 Run 400m

sled_ceiling_test.text: READING IT: line up the 3 rounds - arrival HR vs (sled 25m time) and (metres to settle on the run after). The CEILING is the arrival HR where the sled time JUMPS and/or the run won't settle within ~150m. Race arrival target = ~10-15 bpm BELOW that ceiling. That number then sets the target for sled_entry_rehearsal - MEASURED 12 Sep 2026: run-settle ceiling >173 (settled by ~90m even arriving 173), BUT sled-push time degrades above ~160 arrival (1:11@158 vs 1:26-1:48@172-173). Race arrival target = ~158-160 (push-protective), NOT the 173 run ceiling. Cardiff-141 retired. Re-measure sled time on race kit at the 10 Oct sim.
